hardening_notes: scripts/orchestrator/acp-broker:993-1001: the socket check and the record sweep are two steps, so a listener that binds and writes a record between them (a third broker of the same Router launch, started by the operator just as this one ends) can lose that record; same principal, millisecond window. Re-reading the presence after the glob would close it.

scripts/orchestrator/acp-broker:995: the line names "another broker's listener, or one the relay could not remove" for any standing socket; a relay ended by SIGKILL prints nothing (acp-relay.py:287-291 never runs), so the operator meets a stale socket and records with no relay line; the next take refuses on it (:1074).

scripts/orchestrator/acp-broker:1080-1081: the glob honours an inherited GLOBIGNORE (bash imports it; the parent's probe: GLOBIGNORE=* gives count 0 for a directory with an entry), so a broker started with it set would take a non-empty directory; only the operator, or the lever that starts the broker (U344), sets that environment. `unset GLOBIGNORE` before the glob removes the dependence.
